We may note here that notice has  2 been issued only in so far as the second to fifth appellants are concerned.
3. With the assistance of the learned counsel appearing for the parties, we have perused the statements of material witnesses forming part of the charge-sheet.

We have perused the statement of the second respondent recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, the Cr.P.C.) and her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. by the learned Judicial Magistrate.

There are specific allegations in both the statements against the first appellant of demand of dowry,
cruelty etc.
There is an allegation against the fifth appellant that he inappropriately touched the second respondent.
The allegations made by the second respondent against the second and third appellants are omnibus and very vague.
It is alleged that they instigated the first appellant to demand dowry.
These are generalised allegations.
There is absolutely no allegation against the forth appellant.

This is one of the several cases which are described in paragraph 28 of the judgment of the Coordinate Bench dated 10th December, 2024 in Criminal Appeal No.5199 of 2024 titled as Dara Lakshmi Narayana & Others vs. State Kiran R vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79747496/

sentences.text: The statements of the other witnesses as far as the  3 role played by the second to fourth appellants are concerned are hearsay.
Therefore, continuation of criminal proceedings against the second to fourth appellants will be nothing but an abuse of process of law.
5. As far as fifth appellant is concerned, a contention has been raised that he was a juvenile at the relevant time.
The learned counsel appearing for the appellant has produced on record photocopies of his aadhar card and secondary school certificate which record his date of birth as 17th March, 2003.

The First Information Report at the instance of the second respondent was registered on 24th June, 2020 in relation to the allegations of the incidents spanning over the period between 10th December, 2018 to 24th June, 2020.
Therefore, an inquiry will have to be held by the learned Trial Court on the plea of juvenility raised by the fifth appellant.

6. Accordingly, we modify the impugned judgment and order and quash the proceedings of Criminal Case No.165 of 2021 pending on the file of JMFC, 6th Court, Mangaluru as against the second to forth appellants.
7. We direct the learned Trial Judge to hold an inquiry on the question whether on the date of registration of the offence, fifth appellant was a juvenile in conflict with law.

Inquiry shall be held after giving an opportunity of  4 Kiran R vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79747496/
3 adducing evidence to the parties.
